stories.title: Supplier results show AI demand and margins remain intact despite heavy capex
stories.whatChanged: TSMC reported strong 2026Q3 revenue and 58.7% operating margin; CoreWeave reported large Q2 PPE/capitalised software and positive operating cash flow.
stories.whyItMatters: Verified issuer results show supplier earnings and sizable capex that support ongoing AI infrastructure demand, moderating a narrative of immediate demand collapse.
stories.mechanism: Hyperscaler and AI-lab spending sustains supplier orders and margins even as higher rates raise financing costs; large capex increases near‑term cash needs but does not prove end‑demand collapse.
stories.conclusion: Supplier earnings and reported capex are consistent with continued AI infrastructure demand, but large capex raises funding and cash‑flow questions that require issuer‑level financing and order evidence to resolve.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical issuer disclosures showing material capex cancellations, delayed GPU orders, or sharp downward guidance from hyperscalers would falsify this resilience claim.

stories.title: Long‑end nominal yields high while NY Fed ACM term premium has fallen
stories.whatChanged: 10Y nominal ~5.09% with real 10Y ~2.78% and NY Fed ACM term premium ~0.75% (five‑session −23.7bp).
stories.whyItMatters: Nominal long yields can be elevated because of higher real yields even as modelled term premium compresses; that alters which channel is tightening financial conditions.
stories.mechanism: Real‑rate pressure explains much of nominal 10Y level while term‑premium governance has eased; ongoing auction and supply context could still re‑exert upward pressure if absorption weakens.
stories.conclusion: Current evidence points to a nominal 10Y driven by higher real yields with a falling modelled term premium; auction/supply evidence exists but dealer balance‑sheet and volatility (MOVE) series are missing for a full decomposition.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical dealer position/fails evidence, a rising MOVE index, or repeated weak auction metrics (when‑issued tail evidence) showing persistent stop‑throughs would imply term‑premium or structural demand problems instead.

investigations.question: Did the mid‑October inflation/news sequence materially reprice short‑end policy expectations and persist into later sessions?
investigations.whyItMatters: If front‑end repricing persisted, that implies tighter policy expectations and higher cost of capital for growth sectors.
investigations.currentExplanation: Short end remains elevated (US 2Y 4.74%) while ACM term premium fell; lack of canonical intraday Fed‑funds‑futures and MOVE prevents proving persistence.
investigations.expectedReaction: Conventional: hotter CPI would lift short‑end Fed‑funds repricing and push nominal yields higher.
competingExplanations: Initial short‑end repricing persisted as policy expectations shifted.
Initial short‑end spike faded as auction/flow sequencing rebalanced yields.

verified.title: Long-end Treasury stress
verified.detail: On 24 September 2026, the U.S. Treasury par yield curve closed with the 10-year yield at 5.18% and the 30-year yield at 5.47%, confirming severe long-duration rate pressure.

verified.title: S&P concentration remains extreme
verified.detail: Nvidia and Apple together accounted for more than 15% of the S&P 500, reinforcing the concentration risk behind an index that can remain firm even when participation is weaker.

verified.title: Saudi/Houthi energy risk persists
verified.detail: Saudi-led coalition forces said six Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted on 24 September, with Yanbu among the targeted areas; the report also described claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: Natural-gas storage tightened
verified.detail: EIA reported Lower-48 working gas at 3,351 Bcf for the week ended 18 September 2026, a 53 Bcf weekly injection and 95 Bcf above the five-year average.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.title: META Muse catalyst verified
verified.detail: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent and said it planned integration with smart glasses, independently confirming the product catalyst behind the creator's META discussion.

verified.title: RKLB defence-space catalyst verified
verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.

open.title: Exact Hormuz-for-sanctions deal terms
open.detail: Active US–Iran diplomacy is verified, but the transcript's specific exchange — reopening Hormuz for lifting the economic blockade plus frozen-asset access — is not independently confirmed.

open.detail: Independent work supports late-September weakness in midterm years, but the exact 'week 39 is worst since 1950, -0.5% average, positive under 50%' statistic has not been reproduced from a primary historical series.
